newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Telecom invests $480 mln on local phones.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Telecom invests $480 mln on local phones.

text.p: Colombian state phone company Telecom, in partnership with four foreign private sector firms, will invest $480 million in the local telephone market over the next three years, the company chairman said Tuesday.

Jose Blackburn told Reuters that Telecom would be looking to install 500,000 new lines in the southwest city of Cali, the northwest city of Medellin, the central cities of Manizales and Pereira and the northeast city of Bucaramanga -- with a combined population of about 7 million.
Telecom will carry out the work in partnership with Sweden's Ericsson SpA, Japan's NEC Corp, Canada's Nortel Northern Telecom Ltd and Germany's Siemens AG, Blackburn said.
Until now, Telecom has supplied long-distance and international phone service, while the local phone market has been controlled by companies operated by municipal authorities.
Telecom set up a strategic partnership, known as Capitel, with the four foreign companies in 1996 to install 555,000 phones lines in Bogota at a cost of about $513 million.

Blackburn told Reuters that Telecom's fiber optic trunk network would come into operation by the end of this year and that the company was investing $20 million on satellite communications over the next two years.
Telecom also has a 65 percent stake in a $25 million project to set up a regional television station that would serve 16.5 million people in 14 of Colombia's 33 provinces.
